territorial_scope.description: Applies to high-technology data centers located in Georgia, as defined in the paragraph.

evidence.quote: a facility, campus of facilities, or array of interconnected facilities in this state

summary.short: Exempts high-technology data center equipment from Georgia sales and use tax during July 1, 2018 to December 31, 2031, for qualifying data centers that meet a county-tiered minimum investment threshold and hold a commissioner's certificate.
summary.long: Paragraph 68.1 exempts high-technology data center equipment from Georgia sales and use tax for the period July 1, 2018 to December 31, 2031. The exemption covers computer equipment and related materials, such as backup generators, cooling equipment and power distribution units, used in a data center that meets a minimum investment threshold. The threshold is 25 new quality jobs and $250 million in expenditures in counties over 50,000 population, 10 jobs and $75 million in counties of 30,000 to 50,001, and 5 jobs and $25 million in other counties, measured over any consecutive seven-year period. Sellers must collect the tax unless the buyer holds a commissioner's certificate. The commissioner may issue a certificate only if the data center will more likely than not meet the threshold, may require a bond of up to $20 million, and may revoke the certificate. Data centers must file a final report within 60 days after the end of the seventh year, report annual exempted taxes and jobs, and list their customers. If the threshold is missed, taxes and interest must be repaid within 90 days. Exempt data centers may not claim listed income tax credits. The commissioner must issue implementing rules and an annual report to legislative finance chairs. The paragraph is repealed by operation of law on January 1, 2032.

notes: Only relations, entities and notes were requested; other sections are not annotated here. The text states no enabling act, session-law history or amending act; the enacting legal basis is not in the document. The population bands in (G)(v) are written as 'greater than 50,000', 'greater than 30,000 and less than 50,001', and 'less than 30,001' (2010 census or any future census); they are coded as written. The investment window runs from July 1, 2018 to December 31, 2031, while the seven-year period starts at a chosen exemption start date on or after July 1, 2018, so a period may extend past the window end; the text does not address this. Paragraph (H) states repeal by operation of law on January 1, 2032.
